translationRepairs: Qing Bu rebelled and fled. Han established imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.
Qing Bu rebelled and was destroyed. Han established imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.
亡 describes Qing Bu's destruction after his rebellion, not his flight; the idiomatic translation already preserves the event correctly.
He was then transferred once more to serve as Chancellor of Dai.
He was then transferred again to serve as chancellor to the King of Dai.
相代王 identifies the King of Dai as the ruler Zhang Cang served; the revised wording makes that relationship explicit in natural English.
The proposal turns the telegraphic calque into grammatical English without changing the attribution.
I privately worry about it, and do not know what to do.'
I privately worry about it, and do not know what to do."
The Chinese closes the speech here, so the mismatched single quotation mark should be corrected to a double quotation mark.
Yao say: Your majesty alone should for Zhao wang establish noble strong chancellor, and Lu empress, crown prince, group ministers always what revere fear then can.

Yao said, "Your Majesty should appoint a noble and powerful chancellor for the King of Zhao, one whom Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the ministers have always revered and feared. Only such a man will do."
The source calls for a powerful chancellor whom the court fears and respects; this keeps every element while avoiding the proposal's awkward 'should alone establish.'
The name and speech tag need correction, but the quotation must remain open because Gaozu's speech continues in s0060.
Yao say: Censor grand master Zhou Chang, his person firm endure simple straight, moreover from Lu empress, crown prince and great ministers all always revere fear him.
Yao said, "Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang is firm, resolute, honest, and upright. Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the great ministers have all long revered and feared him.
The proposal correctly repairs the prose, but the quotation must remain open because Yao's answer concludes in s0062.
The proposal restores natural word order and correctly closes the speech that began in s0061.
The proposal correctly joins Gaozu's name and supplies a grammatical speech tag and quotation.
After three years he was dismissed, and Pingyang marquis Cao Jiu was made Censor Grand Master.
After three years he was dismissed, and Cao Zhu, Marquis of Pingyang, was made Censor Grand Master.
窋 is Zhu, and the proposed English title order is both accurate and idiomatic.
In the fifth year before the reign of Emperor Jing, Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
In the fifth year of Emperor Jing's first reign period (152 BC), Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
前五年 is the fifth year of Emperor Jing's first chronological period, not five years before his reign; adding 152 BC makes the date unambiguous in English.
In the fifth year before Xiaojing's reign, Cang died, posthumously titled Marquis Wen.
In the fifth year of Xiaojing's first reign period, Cang died and was posthumously titled Marquis Wen.
The literal translation must treat 前 as the first of Emperor Jing's numbered reign periods, not as a time before his accession.
Initially, Zhang Cang's father was not full five chi in height. When he gave birth to Cang, Cang was over eight chi tall, and became marquis and chancellor.
At first, Zhang Cang's father was less than five chi tall. Yet the son he fathered, Cang, grew to over eight chi tall and became a marquis and chancellor.
The father did not give birth, but the proposal could also imply that Cang was eight chi tall at birth; this wording preserves the contrast and later growth.
Zhang Cang was virtuous to Wang Ling.
Zhang Cang was grateful to Wang Ling.
德 here means that Zhang Cang felt gratitude for Wang Ling's kindness; 'indebted in virtue' is accurate in direction but unnatural English.

Guangguo was worthy and had good conduct, so he wished to make him chancellor. After thinking about it for a long time, he decided it was not possible. Moreover, the great ministers from Gao emperor's time had mostly died, and there were no suitable ones remaining. So he made Censor Grand Master Jia chancellor, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guan according to his old fief.

Guangguo was worthy and upright, so the emperor wished to make him chancellor. After long deliberation, however, he decided it was impossible. Most of the senior ministers from Emperor Gao's time had already died, and none of those remaining appeared suitable. He therefore made Censor Grand Master Jia chancellor and, on the basis of his former fief, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gu'an.
故安 is Gu'an, and the surrounding literal prose also benefits from grammatical subjects and natural official-title phrasing.
Until court of ritual, not can not solemn!"
As for the rites of court, they cannot but be kept solemn!"
不可以不肅 is an emphatic requirement that court rites be solemn; the proposal renders it clearly and closes the speech correctly.
Afterwards, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Then Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen to serve as doctor, drafted the calendar system for earth virtue, and changed the first year.

Afterward, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Emperor Wen then summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an Erudite, ordered him to draft a calendar and institutions based on the virtue of Earth, and inaugurated a new first year.
博士 is Erudite, and Emperor Wen remains the subject who appoints Gongsun Chen, orders the drafting, and inaugurates the new calendar.
Chancellor You Che was a man from Changling.
There was Chancellor Che, who was a man from Changling.
有 introduces Chancellor Che; it is not the surname You. The proposal matches the Chinese syntax and the idiomatic translation.
Chancellor Wei was a worthy man, a person from Lu.
Chancellor Wei Xian was a person from Lu.
賢 is Chancellor Wei's personal name in the identifying construction, not an adjective describing him.

At that time Jing Zhao prefect Zhao Jun was memorialized by the chancellor to be exempted from crime. He sent people to arrest Chancellor Wei, wishing to seek escape from crime, but Wei did not listen.

At that time the Prefect of the Capital, Zhao Jun, was memorialized by the chancellor for removal on criminal charges. He sent men to seize Chancellor Wei, hoping to escape punishment, but Wei would not yield.
The surrounding coercion shows that 趙君 faced removal and punishment; 免罪 cannot mean that the chancellor sought to exempt him from guilt.
Grant the rank of Guan Nei marquis, one hundred catties of yellow gold.'
He was granted the rank of Marquis Within the Pass and one hundred catties of gold."
The source records two passive grants; 'gold' is natural English for 黃金, and the sentence closes the quoted decree.
Censor Grand Master Xue Jun was exempted, and he became Censor Grand Master.
The Censor Grand Master, Master Xue, was dismissed, and Wei Xuancheng became Censor Grand Master.
免 means dismissal; the omitted subject is Wei Xuancheng from the surrounding biography, and 薛君 is the honorific 'Master Xue,' not a personal name Xue Jun.
His talent descended, he shot at the policy questions several times without hitting, until the ninth time, then he hit the Bing grade.
His abilities were mediocre; he sat the policy examinations several times without passing, and only on the ninth attempt did he achieve the third-class grade.
才下 describes mediocre ability, while 射策 and 中丙科 describe repeated policy examinations and a third-class result.
He supplemented as Pingyuan literature graduated secretary.
He was appointed as a Literary Clerk in Pingyuan commandery.
補 marks appointment and 文學卒史 is the office of Literary Clerk; the proposed wording removes opaque calques.

Xiaoyuan was fond of Poetry, so he was moved to be Guanglu Xun, dwelling in the palace as teacher, teaching and instructing those on left and right, while county officials sat by his side listening, very much praising it, daily becoming more honored and noble.

Emperor Yuan was fond of the Book of Songs, so Heng was promoted to Superintendent of the Imperial Household. He lived in the palace as a teacher and instructed those around him, while the emperor sat beside him and listened. The emperor esteemed him highly, and he grew more honored by the day.
縣官 denotes the sovereign here, not county officials; the revision also identifies 孝元 and renders 詩 and 光祿勳 in clear English.
Censor Grand Master Zheng Hong was exempted for matters, and Gentleman Kuang became Censor Grand Master.
Censor Grand Master Zheng Hong was dismissed for misconduct, and Kuang Heng became Censor Grand Master.
坐事免 means dismissal for an offense, and 匡君 refers to Kuang Heng, the subject of the surrounding biography.
